clearedSpotChecks.check: MegaETH. The KeylessDeploy sandbox is the one feature on the 21 networks with shape A: it runs caller-chosen init code in a second EVM with a new journal over live state and merges the resulting state into the parent. Can an ordinary contract start it from inside a call, and is transient state merged back.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I fetched system/intercept.rs, sandbox/mod.rs, sandbox/execution.rs, sandbox/state.rs and sandbox/state_merge.rs from the main branch of megaeth-labs/mega-evm (workspace version 1.7.3, revm 40.0.3). KeylessDeployInterceptor::intercept returns without acting when ctx.is_inside_sandbox() is true or depth is not zero (intercept.rs line 301) and when the call target is not the KeylessDeploy address (line 305). The module text in sandbox/mod.rs states the same rule and names the NotIntercepted() fallback for calls from contracts. execute_keyless_deploy_sandbox builds a SandboxDb over journal.inner.state and the database (execution.rs line 583), marks the new context with with_inside_sandbox(true) (line 646) and runs transact_raw on a new MegaEvm (line 650). The word transient occurs in none of execution.rs, state.rs and state_merge.rs, so the inner run starts with an empty map and nothing is copied back. I repeated the on-chain test on https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc near block 32,597,064 (client mega-reth/v2.2.3-72527bc). eth_call to 0x6342000000000000000000000000000000000003 with selector 0x846365d5 (keylessDeploy(bytes,uint256), computed here) and a one byte payload reverted with data 0xae1270d3, which is the selector of MalformedEncoding(). The same calldata sent from a creation frame returned a zero success flag and return data 0x1894f076, which is the selector of NotIntercepted(). A sandbox therefore starts only as the first frame of a transaction addressed to KeylessDeploy. No PoolManager code has run in the parent at that point, so no unlock flag, delta or synced reserves value exists outside the sandbox (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114, 279-288), and inside the sandbox every call shares one map. Not confirmed: which mega-evm revision mega-reth v2.2.3 pins, and whether the node accepts any transaction type with more than one frame at depth zero. The research file already lists both as a lead.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Tempo. Type 0x76 batches, precompiles that might call out to contracts, the storage credit settlement that removes transient slots, T14 configurable accounts and the zone contracts. For each: can a contract start it from inside a call, which transient map does it use, and are transient writes journaled like storage writes.
clearedSpotChecks.note: The node reports tempo/v1.19.0-697ea97, and Cargo.toml at that commit pins evm2 at 66687c18 (lines 322 to 324). In crates/evm/src/handler.rs execute_batch takes one checkpoint (line 1289), runs each call as an initial frame from the signer, and rolls the whole batch back when one call fails (line 1339). In evm2 state/mod.rs TSTORE pushes a TransientStorageChange journal entry (lines 806 to 836), rollback restores it (lines 891 to 898) and clear_transaction_state empties the map (lines 523 to 539). take_transient_storage (lines 842 to 859) removes slots without a journal entry, and its one caller in handler/config.rs passes STORAGE_CREDITS_ADDRESS (lines 452 to 454) after a successful result, so PoolManager slots are not touched. The precompile storage trait in crates/precompiles/src/storage/mod.rs offers sload, sstore, tload, tstore, events, gas and checkpoints and has no function that calls a contract. The T14 opcode handler in crates/evm/src/instructions.rs (lines 143 to 180) serves a configurable account through the same storage context with native code. T14 is not active: eth_getCode at 0xAACC000000000000000000000000000000000000 returned 0x near block 50,349,790, while 0x1060000000000000000000000000000000000000 returned 0xef. crates/contracts/src/precompiles/mod.rs lines 67 to 68 give that address for the configurable account, and crates/evm/src/block.rs lines 853 to 854 deploy the marker at the T14 boundary. One point the research file does not mention: evm2 at the pinned revision contains State::committed_copy (state/mod.rs lines 127 to 150). Its comment says the result has the running transaction's writes committed and an empty transaction scratch, and that it serves as the base state of a transaction nested in the running one. That is shape A as a library facility. I found no call to committed_copy or call_tx in handler.rs, handler/config.rs, instructions.rs, evm.rs, block.rs, common.rs, action_replay.rs, engine.rs, fee_manager.rs, or in the precompile lib.rs and storage/mod.rs at 697ea97. I could not search the whole tree, because the archive download and the GitHub API are refused here. A lead below asks for that search. The revert probe passed on the Tempo RPC node in my own run.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Arc. On-chain test of the CallFrom precompile at 0x1800000000000000000000000000000000000003: does the child call it starts see the transient storage of the surrounding transaction, and are the child's transient writes kept. Earlier cycles answered from the main branch source only.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I wrote my own probe and ran it with state overrides on https://rpc.mainnet.arc.io near block 32,650,144 (client arc/v1). A counter contract returns its transient slot 2 and adds 0x22. Code placed at the Multicall3From address 0x522fAf9A91c41c443c66765030741e4AaCe147D0 called the counter directly, then through callFrom (selector 0x1595ec0b), then directly again. The readings were 0, 0x22 and 0x44, both with tx.origin and with the helper as the substituted sender. The same code at an address outside the allowlist got the revert string unauthorized caller, and its two direct readings were 0 and 0x22. I added a case the research file did not run: a callFrom child that calls the counter and then reverts. The precompile returned success false with the child's reading 0x22, and the next direct reading was 0x22, so the reverted child's transient write was undone. In crates/evm/src/evm.rs on main, init_subcall rejects a substituted sender that is neither the calling helper nor the transaction signer (lines 948 to 956), takes a checkpoint from the running journal (line 1039), and a rejected or failed child is rolled back through that checkpoint (lines 1230 to 1231). The child shares the PoolManager's lock flag, deltas and synced reserves with its parent, so neither shape exists here. The deployed arc-node revision is not confirmed, and the on-chain result agrees with the main branch.

clearedSpotChecks.check: On-chain test on all 21 RPC endpoints: is transient storage restored on every way a frame can fail, and is it restored to the earlier nonzero value. The earlier critic probe covered REVERT. This probe creates a child contract and calls it so that the child writes transient slot 1 and then ends with REVERT, with INVALID, by running out of gas in a loop, and with REVERT after a nested call that itself succeeded and wrote slot 2. It then lets a write succeed, repeats the reverting call, and runs the same writes through DELEGATECALL against the parent's own slot.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I disassembled the 485 byte payload from the research file (sha256 prefix 940d9cbc7584c3a8) and it does what the item says. The child dispatches on the first calldata byte: 1 writes 0x11 and reverts, 2 writes 0x22 and hits INVALID, 3 writes 0x33 and loops until gas runs out, 4 writes 0x44, calls itself with mode 9 (which writes 0x99 to slot 2 and stops) and reverts, 5 writes 0x55 and stops, 6 returns slots 1 and 2. The parent then sets its own slot to 0xaa and repeats modes 1, 2 and 5 through DELEGATECALL. I sent it with eth_call and no to address to the rpc URL of each of the 21 networks on 2026-11-23 (for example Ethereum at block 26,474,285, Tempo at 50,349,565, HyperEVM at 51,989,444). Every endpoint returned the child address followed by the same 15 words: 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0x55, 0, 0x55, 0, 0xaa, 0xaa, 0x55. The return data holds 16 words, since the first word is the address of the created child, and the item counts the 15 that follow. A take debit or a settle credit written in a frame that fails is undone together with that frame's transfers on every RPC node (src/PoolManager.sol:294-295, 364, src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:26-39). The result describes the RPC node of each network. On Celo the endpoint answers from two different clients, see the next item.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Celo. The fee currency calls debitGasFees and creditGasFees that the node makes around a CIP-64 transaction. Can a contract start them, which transient map do they use, and is anything discarded between them and the main call.
clearedSpotChecks.note: The conclusion holds, and one statement in the item is true for only one of the two Celo clients. Twelve web3_clientVersion requests to https://forno.celo.org returned reth/v2.2.0-74cc8bb eight times and Geth/v0.1.0-untagged-c7ed55b8 four times, and docs.celo.org names celo-reth from celo-org/celo-kona as the execution client. The item read only the op-geth fork. For op-geth I confirmed at commit c7ed55b8 that innerExecute calls StateDB.Prepare at core/state_transition.go line 602, runs preCheck with the debit at line 605, and calls contracts.CreditFees at line 824. In celo-revm on the main branch of celo-kona the picture differs. The debit runs through the non-committing system call inside a journal checkpoint, and on success the handler clears the whole transient map (handler.rs lines 665 to 698). The credit runs in build_execution_result after the main frame has finished (handler.rs line 937) through the committing call (contracts/erc20.rs line 134), which ends in commit_tx and then clears the whole transient map again (contracts/core_contracts.rs lines 243 to 247). The sentence that nothing clears transient storage between the debit, the main call and the credit is therefore wrong for celo-reth. The safety result does not change. On both clients the debit runs before any code of the main call and the credit runs after the main frame has returned, when unlock has closed the lock and every delta is zero (src/PoolManager.sol:112-113). The committing call has one call site, the credit, so no opcode or precompile lets a contract reach it during a call. An earlier cleared item of the Celo unit already recorded the celo-revm behaviour. Not confirmed: which celo-kona revision the mainnet nodes run, since 74cc8bb does not resolve in that repository.

leads.question: Does any crate of tempoxyz/tempo at commit 697ea97, or any later release that mainnet adopts, call evm2 State::committed_copy, Evm::call_tx or Evm::transact from inside a precompile, an opcode handler or a transaction handler while a user call is still running?
leads.why: evm2 at the pinned revision 66687c18 ships committed_copy (crates/evm2/src/evm/state/mod.rs lines 127 to 150), documented as the base state of a transaction nested in the running one: the running transaction's writes are committed and the transient map is empty. A feature built on it that a contract can start from inside a call would let a caller sync a token outside, pay, settle and mint a claim inside, and settle again outside for the same tokens (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 322-329, 349-364). I found no call site in the eleven files of crates/evm and crates/precompiles that I read, and a full tree search was not possible in this session.

leads.question: Which celo-kona revision do the Celo mainnet nodes run, and do op-geth c7ed55b8 and celo-reth produce the same result when a listed fee currency or adapter leaves a nonzero transient slot at the end of debitGasFees?
leads.why: op-geth keeps transient writes of the debit visible to the main call (core/state_transition.go lines 602 to 605), while celo-revm clears the whole transient map after the debit (crates/celo-revm/src/handler.rs lines 665 to 698). The PoolManager is unaffected in both cases because its lock is closed and its deltas are zero outside unlock (src/PoolManager.sol:112-113). A difference between the two clients would be a chain level fault that delays PoolManager transactions, and this cycle's Celo clearance for the theme was written from the op-geth source alone.
